content:
I’ve been using Day One for a few years now, and I’ve varied my use of it overtime from something I needed to confide in, to a recordkeeping tool, regular journal, basically whatever I needed. The best part about it is for all my different needs, you can just create a different journal and have all these different journals accessible within the app. 

It is easy to go back and find older entries or specific events or mentions or things using the search function. You can also custom tag entries which is handy. I also like that it has a “on this day” feature that will show you entries from this day from previous years. 

Sometimes I type my entries out, and sometimes I dictate my entries and go back and fix them up real quick with the keyboard, but you can also put in video entries, which I don’t do much, but I do upload a lot of photos. You can also have your entries printed out over whatever time range you want if you would like hardcopies as well. 

It’s only slightly higher priced than a hardcopy journal, and yet it comes with so, so, so many more features. It syncs across all my devices and I use it all the time, any time, anywhere. I highly recommend this journal.

title: Privacy now gone?
content:
[UPDATE] My prediction has come true. Gone is the brilliant support you used to get. Now, you receive an email that simply says “Read the help guides”. If your answer is not found, reply to this email and we’ll get back to you in 48 hours. Gee thanks!

title: Finally
content: After years of using Evernote for diary entries, which was great, but not really fit for purpose, I thought to myself, I want something really simple. Maybe I could pay a developer to make it for me? But first look around, right? It wasn’t immediately obvious Day One was a fit from the external reviews, there are a lot of diary apps out there that aren’t meant for writers, or people who are already serious about keeping a journal. But I’ve only been in it a few days and you’d have to screw up to lose me. The platform is great for creating (I haven’t got into syncing or password issues yet). The thing I was really looking for was something that pointed me back to posts from years past, talking about the same subjects, etc, as a reminder and a pointer to what is more meaningful over time. And it was there. (I’d like a subject matter reminder as well, hopefully some AI will help out on that in the future.) I think my favourite feature though is the photos, my photo feed is probably a more meaningful diary than the words I remember to write. Now I can not only capture my thoughts at the end of the day but put context around the images from the day as well, which in turn generate new and often betting thinking. The only issue now is transferring over many hundreds of Evernote diary entries, which is fine and easy enough to do, one-by-one. As I do them the old photos from the stream pop up and I want to add some words to contextualise them - but when I tap the pics they don’t go to the day, they come back to the present and you have to scroll back through a year or more of pics to find the one you were looking for. So developers, small thing I know, but I suspect those serious diarists who are new to Day One will appreciate a quick look at this.

title: Not here for it
content:
I've been using this app daily since 2013. I happily transitioned from version 1 to version 2. This app has been invaluable for me, keeping track of memories and milestones. My progress through rough patches and my ups and downs. I occasionally look through my older entries, and to see how life has progressed captures an emotion that can't be explained.

Whilst version 2 made some questionable UI and UX decisions, overall the additions and enhancements (and constant iteration) made the quirks manageable. I was a content user. I was confident that my extremely personal data would be kept safe and secure, especially with end-to-end encryption (let's just say, I'd much rather someone get my credit card details than my Day One entries...)

Now, you've gone ahead and slapped an ugly $54 annual subscription onto this beautiful little app.

Okay, so I'm genuinely curious: what made you think people would be happy to spend $4.49 A MONTH on an app that cost that much, one-time, up-front, a week ago?

To add insult to injury, you've put us non-subscription ("Plus") users on 'maintenance mode': all we're going to get are 'bug fixes'. No new features. No feature requests.

I don't want to see this app fail. It's become a part of my memory and recollection process. Maybe you'll have to hit rock bottom to see just how good things were.

Sadly, I don't see you reversing this ill-advised decision, evidently made in the insular bubble of the tech blogosphere which applauds this short-sighted business model.

Nothing I can say or do will affect this decision (or a reversal of it). Just know you've severely, personally disappointed someone.

author: Zack . D

title: Not here for it
content:
I've been using this app daily since 2013. I happily transitioned from version 1 to version 2. This app has been invaluable for me, keeping track of memories and milestones. My progress through rough patches and my ups and downs. I occasionally look through my older entries, and to see how life has progressed captures an emotion that can't be explained.

Whilst version 2 made some questionable UI and UX decisions, overall the additions and enhancements (and constant iteration) made the quirks manageable. I was a content user. I was confident that my extremely personal data would be kept safe and secure, especially with end-to-end encryption (let's just say, I'd much rather someone get my credit card details than my Day One entries...)

Now, you've gone ahead and slapped an ugly $54 annual subscription onto this beautiful little app.

Okay, so I'm genuinely curious: what made you think people would be happy to spend $4.49 A MONTH on an app that cost that much, one-time, up-front, a week ago?

To add insult to injury, you've put us non-subscription ("Plus") users on 'maintenance mode': all we're going to get are 'bug fixes'. No new features. No feature requests.

I don't want to see this app fail. It's become a part of my memory and recollection process. Maybe you'll have to hit rock bottom to see just how good things were.

Sadly, I don't see you reversing this ill-advised decision, evidently made in the insular bubble of the tech blogosphere which applauds this short-sighted business model.

Nothing I can say or do will affect this decision (or a reversal of it). Just know you've severely, personally disappointed someone.
